candidate: OpenRA route: OpenRA/ra2 (official RA2 mod for the OpenRA C# engine) + hel1o-wor1d/OpenRA2 (fork)
summary: Both repos exist and are GPL-3.0. OpenRA/ra2 is a native desktop (C#/.NET + SDL2 + OpenGL) mod that calls itself a "pre-alpha" "developer preview" in its own main-menu notice. It is multiplayer/skirmish only: there is no campaign, no Yuri's Revenge content, and it runs a basic "Test AI". Several RA2 units are missing (V3, Dreadnought, Siege Chopper), and only one building (Washington Monument) can be garrisoned. FMV and INI modding are not supported. It is pinned to the 2023 engine (release-20231010), and its current master crashes loading The Alamo map (issue #826, Aug 2026). The PR that moves it to the 2025 engine (#814) has been open since April 2025. Development is essentially dormant: 2 commits in 2024 and 23 in 2025 (all maintenance), with the last code commit on 2025-11-28. hel1o-wor1d/OpenRA2 is upstream as of 2023-03-21 plus 5 README-only commits, 25 commits behind, and adds a OneDrive link to download the game files. It is not a real alternative and has a legal red flag. On the positive side, the OpenRA engine is healthy (17.4k stars, pushed 2026-09-25, now on .NET 10). It has good multiplayer, replay, save and map-editor infrastructure, proven HD-sprite support (TiberianDawnHD), and post-processing passes since release-20250330. However, OpenRA has no official or open-source browser build. The only working browser port (Rosebud, April 2026) is closed-source, supports Red Alert 1 only, and has known shroud rendering bugs. The GitLab "openra-wasm-port" is an empty README stub. For a web-based, faithful RA2 HD remaster this route would require three big efforts: (a) finishing large parts of RA2 gameplay, (b) porting a C# engine to WebAssembly and WebGL2, and (c) forking the engine for custom shaders. It is a weak primary base but a useful reference and fallback.
license_evidence: VERIFIED: GitHub API reports license GPL-3.0 for OpenRA/ra2, hel1o-wor1d/OpenRA2 and OpenRA/OpenRA. The LICENSE file in both clones is the GNU GPL v3 (29 June 2007). The C# headers (e.g. OpenRA.Mods.RA2/UtilityCommands/ImportRA2MapCommand.cs) say "GNU General Public License ... either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version", so strictly it is GPL-3.0-or-later. The mod ships no EA art: it requires the user's own ra2.mix, language.mix and theme.mix (mods/ra2/mod.yaml ModContent; installer sources are CD, Origin and First Decade, with no Steam source, see issue #810). INFERENCE: a web deployment serves the compiled WASM to users, so it counts as distribution under GPLv3 and the full source of any engine or mod fork must be published. That is fine for an open project but rules out a closed product. EA's Feb-2025 GPL source release covered TD, RA1, Renegade and Generals but not RA2 or TS (https://www.engadget.com/gaming/pc/ea-releases-source-code-for-four-command--conquer-games-223425774.html), so RA2 assets remain EA-owned and must come from the user's copy. Red flag: hel1o-wor1d/OpenRA2's README adds a "Download from OneDriver" link for the game under "official places". It is likely unauthorized redistribution of EA files; I did not open it.
provenance: OpenRA/ra2 is original community work (the OpenRA team, 2015 onward), built on OpenRA's shared TS/RA2 "2.5D" engine code. It is not derived from Chrono Divide. hel1o-wor1d/OpenRA2 is a GitHub fork of OpenRA/ra2 (parent=OpenRA/ra2) whose only changes are to the README.
provenance_evidence: VERIFIED via git: the first OpenRA/ra2 commit is f17fa90 (2015-04-10, Taryn Hill, "Move ra2 mod into ra2 directory. Add openra engine submodule"). There are 1162 commits from 46 authors (top: abcdefg30 397, Matthias Mailänder 254+56, Mustafa Alperen Seki 200). hel1o-wor1d/OpenRA2: the GitHub API says fork=true, parent=OpenRA/ra2, created and pushed 2023-07-02. Merge-base with upstream is 2a29249 (2023-03-21). It has exactly 5 extra commits, all "Update README.md" by iamybj on 2023-07-02, and `git diff --stat upstream/master...HEAD` shows README.md only (+53/-4). It is 25 commits behind upstream and still pins ENGINE_VERSION="release-20230225" (upstream pins release-20231010). All C# is OpenRA-style: namespace OpenRA.Mods.RA2, trait/YAML architecture, GPL headers. There is no JS/TS code, so no Chrono Divide lineage.
tech_stack: The engine is OpenRA, written in C#. Bleed targets net10.0 with LangVersion 13 (Directory.Build.props). The release-20231010 engine that the mod uses targets net6.0, which is end-of-life; open PR #827 bumps the mod to dotnet 10. Native dependencies: SDL2 (OpenRA-SDL2-CS), OpenAL (OpenRA-OpenAL-CS), FreeType (OpenRA-Freetype6) and Lua 5.1 via OpenRA-Eluant. Rendering is OpenGL 3.2 Core, GLES 3.0 or ANGLE (Sdl2PlatformWindow.cs), with GLSL "140" or "300 es" (Shader.cs). Game data is MiniYAML rules, sequences and weapons (about 15k lines in mods/ra2). Custom mod code is OpenRA.Mods.RA2, 37 C# files and about 5.2k LOC. Networking is raw TCP lockstep with a threaded server and connection (OpenRA.Game/Network/Connection.cs, Server/Server.cs). Build is a Makefile plus fetch-engine.sh, which downloads the engine zip for ENGINE_VERSION. macOS osx-arm64 builds are supported (engine packaging/macos/buildpackage.sh). No web or JS stack exists.
renderer_architecture:
All VERIFIED from the engine bleed source in scratchpad/repos/openra-engine-bleed unless marked otherwise.

- **Decoding (mods/ra2/mod.yaml):**
  - SpriteFormats: ShpTS, TmpTS, ShpTD, PngSheet. SHP and TMP are decoded to 8-bit indexed sprites by OpenRA.Mods.Common/SpriteLoaders/ShpTSLoader.cs and OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/SpriteLoaders/TmpTSLoader.cs.
  - MIX archives and AudioBag are handled by OpenRA.Mods.RA2/FileSystem/BagFile.cs.
  - VXL and HVA go through OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/Graphics/VoxelLoader.cs (ModelSequenceFormat: VoxelModelSequence).
  - Palettes are PaletteFromFile entries (isotem/isosno/isourb/unittem/city*/lib* .pal) in mods/ra2/rules/palettes.yaml, uploaded into a HardwarePalette texture (OpenRA.Game/Graphics/HardwarePalette.cs). Player colours use the PlayerColorPalette remap of indices 16-31.
- **Map grid:** RectangularIsometric, TileSize 60,30, EnableDepthBuffer: true, MaximumTerrainHeight: 16.
- **Drawing:**
  - OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SpriteRenderer.cs batches sprites across up to 8 texture sheets per draw call (SheetCount = 8), with blend-mode spans in one vertex buffer.
  - glsl/combined.frag does the palette lookup in-shader (`texture(Palette, …)`), optional paletted bilinear "pixel-art scaling", hue-range ColorShift for non-paletted RGBA sprites (the HD player-colour path), per-vertex tint, and per-sprite depth offsets from "DepthSprite" textures (the RA2 mod uses isodepth.shp for buildings; 23 DepthSprite refs).
  - Voxels are rendered by OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/Traits/World/ModelRenderer.cs into offscreen framebuffer sheets with glsl/model.frag. That is per-pixel Lambert lighting from a normals-palette (AmbientLight + DiffuseLight·max(dot(N,L),0)), then composited as sprites.
- **World framebuffer:** Renderer.cs renders the world into an FBO at 1:1 world-pixel scale, then scales it to the screen. Per the code comment, "Mods that use the depth buffer must instead limit their artwork resolution or maximum zoom-out levels". This matters for HD RA2.
- **Lighting and weather:**
  - TerrainLighting is per-cell ambient/RGB tint plus TerrainLightSource lamps (8 uses in the RA2 rules). The upstream Gen2 map importer imports the [Lighting] section.
  - Weather is WeatherOverlay: CPU particles drawn as squares or lines. The RA2 lightning storm uses a custom WeatherPaletteEffect palette shift.
- **Post-processing:** IRenderPostProcessPass with AfterActors, AfterWorld, AfterShroud and AfterAnnotations hooks (WorldRenderer.cs), plus RenderPostProcessPassBase. It is fullscreen-quad based, with existing passes for flash, tint, chronoshift, menufade, sonic and vortex. It is only in release-20250330 and later: the GitHub contents API shows glsl/ at release-20231010 has only combined.* and model.*. So the RA2 mod, pinned to 20231010, cannot use it without the stalled engine bump (#814/#828).
- **Custom shaders:** shaders load only from Platform.EngineDir/glsl (ShaderBindings.GetShaderCode), so custom shaders mean patching or forking the engine.
- **Backends:** no WebGL or WebGPU and no Metal backend. On macOS it runs through Apple's deprecated OpenGL (or ANGLE). INFERENCE: the GLES 3.0 / GLSL "300 es" path maps almost 1:1 to WebGL2, which is the most useful fact for any browser port.

build_result:
Not attempted.

- **No toolchain:** there is no .NET SDK or Mono on this Mac (`which dotnet mono` returned nothing; no ~/.dotnet or /usr/local/share/dotnet). Installing one means downloading and running the Microsoft SDK installer, plus the engine zip and NuGet and native packages that `make` fetches. That needs the user's explicit approval, which this subagent cannot get.
- **No game files:** there are no RA2 .mix files on the machine, so even a successful compile could not be run past the content-install screen.
- **Commands the user can approve later:**
  1. Install a .NET SDK. 6 is end-of-life, so use 8 or 10, with DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=LatestMajor as the fork README suggests, or apply PR #827.
  2. `cd scratchpad/repos/openra-ra2 && make` (downloads OpenRA release-20231010 and builds osx-arm64).
  3. Copy ra2.mix, language.mix and theme.mix into ~/Library/Application Support/OpenRA/Content/ra2/.
  4. Run `./launch-game.sh`.
- **Expected outcome from public reports:** it builds and launches, but some skirmish maps (at least The Alamo) crash on current master (issue #826). A June-2026 Arch Linux log in that issue shows the mod starting on .NET CLR 6.0.36 with "SDL 2 with OpenGL (Modern)".
- **Browser build:** there is no build target or documentation for WASM anywhere in these repos.

asset_requirements: Required: the original RA2 game files from the user's own legal copy. TestFiles are ra2.mix and language.mix; theme.mix is optional for music. The mod also mounts optional sub-mixes (multi, audio, cache, cameo, conquer, generic, isogen, isosnow, isotemp, isourb, load, local, neutral, sidec01/02, sno, snow, tem, temperat, urb, urban, audio.bag), which normally sit inside ra2.mix. They go in ~/Library/Application Support/OpenRA/Content/ra2/ on macOS. The in-game installer only knows the original CD, Origin/EA "Ultimate Collection" (Windows registry) and "The First Decade", not Steam (#810). On a Mac, copy files manually from a Steam or EA install, for example via a Windows machine or CrossOver. YR files (ra2md.mix, expandmd01.mix) are not used at all. No assets are bundled beyond about 15 small UI or placeholder SHPs and PNGs in mods/ra2/bits and uibits. For HD work: TiberianDawnHD relies on the official C&C Remastered assets, but no official HD RA2 art exists, so every HD sprite, tile and voxel replacement must be newly created (AI-generated, re-rendered or hand-made) and must match RA2 isometric footprints, facings (8, 16 or 32) and depth maps.
hd_extensibility:
Effort is rated Low, Medium or High. VERIFIED facts are cited by engine file; the rest is INFERENCE.

1. **Hi-res sprites (Medium–High).** The engine already supports 32-bit art (PngSheet, Tga, Dds loaders in OpenRA.Mods.Common/SpriteLoaders), a per-sequence Scale field (DefaultSpriteSequence.cs:142), hue-based player colour for RGBA art (ColorShift in glsl/combined.frag) and large BGRA sheets. TiberianDawnHD (https://github.com/OpenRA/TiberianDawnHD, engine playtest-20260222) proves the pattern:
   - The mod sets MapGrid TileSize to 128,128 (classic TD is 24) with EnableFrameBufferDownscale and BgraSheetSize 8192.
   - A custom RemasterSpriteSequence (OpenRA.Mods.Mobius/RemasterSpriteSequence.cs) upscales classic art by classicUpscaleFactor, alongside RemasterTerrain and RemasterTerrainRenderer.
   - For RA2 the same approach means changing TileSize from 60,30 to about 240,120 and writing an isometric HD sequence and terrain loader in OpenRA.Mods.RA2.
   - HD terrain must cover TMP ramps and cliffs across 16 height levels, and HD buildings need matching HD DepthSprite maps, because RA2 uses EnableDepthBuffer.
   - Renderer.cs explicitly warns that depth-buffer mods "must instead limit their artwork resolution or maximum zoom-out levels". That makes RA2 HD harder than TD HD.
2. **Voxel-to-mesh (High).** Voxels go through ModelRenderer.cs, VoxelLoader.cs and glsl/model.frag into offscreen sheets. The easy route is to pre-render HD sprite sheets offline, for example Blender renders of re-meshed voxels, and feed them as sprite sequences. A real glTF path needs a new IModel/IModelCache plus shaders in an engine fork.
3. **Normal and depth lighting (High).** combined.frag already samples a per-sprite depth channel, so extending it with a normal-map channel and dynamic lights (explosions, lamps from TerrainLightSource.cs) requires engine shader and ShaderBindings changes. Shaders load only from EngineDir/glsl (ShaderBindings.cs:52), which means maintaining an engine fork.
4. **Post-processing (Low–Medium once on release-20250330 or later).** Implement IRenderPostProcessPass via RenderPostProcessPassBase (OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/RenderPostProcessPassBase.cs) with hooks AfterActors, AfterWorld, AfterShroud and AfterAnnotations (WorldRenderer.cs:299-384). Good candidates are colour grading, bloom, tone mapping and heat haze; the existing flash, tint and chronoshift passes are templates. Blocked until the mod leaves release-20231010 (#814/#828).
5. **Water (High).** Water is plain TMP tiles. It needs a water-mask layer and shader pass for reflections, normals, foam and shoreline, via a new world-layer trait plus an engine shader, reading terrain type "Water".
6. **Weather (Medium).** WeatherOverlay.cs is simple CPU particles, and WeatherPaletteEffect.cs (RA2 mod) is a palette flash. Better options are an AfterWorld post pass (rain streaks, fog, wet-surface grading) and TerrainLighting time-of-day. Issue #684 already proposes gradual GlobalLighting shifts.
7. **Particles, hits and explosions (Medium).** There is no GPU particle system. Effects are sprite animations and IEffect objects (weapons/explosions.yaml, custom ElectricBoltRenderable.cs, RadBeamRenderable.cs, ArcRenderable.cs). The fastest upgrade is HD flipbook sprites with additive BlendMode; a real GPU particle renderer needs engine work.
8. **Browser delivery (Very High).** A browser version needs all of the following:
   - .NET 10 browser-wasm, with SDL2, OpenAL and FreeType via Emscripten.
   - Replacing native Lua (Eluant) with MoonSharp.
   - Replacing TCP (Network/Connection.cs, Server/Server.cs) with WebSocket or WebRTC.
   - Reworking ThreadedGraphicsContext and other threads.
   - Replacing filesystem and user-supplied MIX loading with browser storage.
   
   It is feasible in principle. Rosebud did exactly this for RA1 (https://lab.rosebud.ai/engineering/porting-openra-to-the-browser, April 2026: MoonSharp, WebRTC data channels, shroud-corruption bug unresolved, no source released), and .NET+SDL/OpenGL games run in browsers (https://github.com/MercuryWorkshop/celeste-wasm). pchote's 2020 view was that mono-wasm reached only 1-5 FPS (https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/issues/17836); modern .NET 10 AOT is untested for OpenRA here.
risks: It is not a web base. There is no official or open-source OpenRA browser build. The only working port (Rosebud, RA1 only, April 2026) is closed-source, which also looks inconsistent with GPLv3, and it has an unresolved shroud rendering bug. The GitLab 'openra-wasm-port' is a README stub with no WASM code (verified by grepping the clone). A browser port of the engine would be a multi-month project in its own right.
The RA2 mod is self-declared pre-alpha and dormant. There are no code commits in 2026, and the engine-upgrade PR #814 has been unmerged for 17 months. We would effectively become its maintainers.

Large functionality gaps against the checklist: no Allied or Soviet campaign, no YR, a weak 'Test AI', no Bink FMV, near-zero garrisoning, missing V3/Dreadnought/Siege Chopper, no INI modding, and map import only by conversion without triggers. Step 1 ('original functionality first') would take a long time.

Fidelity to the original: OpenRA reimplements gameplay with its own semantics (pathfinding, production queues, targeting, AI, balance). It will not feel exactly like RA2 without extensive rule tuning; Romanov's Vengeance shows the community drifting toward rebalanced variants.
Current master crashes on at least one bundled skirmish map (issue #826, The Alamo). The fix sits in the unmerged PRs #814/#815.

It is pinned to engine release-20231010 on .NET 6 (end-of-life). That engine lacks the post-processing infrastructure (verified via the GitHub contents API), so an engine bump is a prerequisite for any modern visuals.
Custom shaders load only from the engine's glsl directory, so the HD work requires a maintained engine fork that must be rebased on upstream.

The depth-buffered isometric renderer explicitly limits artwork resolution and zoom-out. The HD tile-size change (60x30 to about 240x120) touches every sequence offset and every map, which is riskier than TD HD's square grid.
macOS runs on Apple's deprecated OpenGL, with no Metal backend, which limits the '2026-level' effects ceiling on the user's M5 Pro unless the app runs via ANGLE or WebGL in a browser.

Legal: RA2 assets are EA-owned and not part of EA's 2025 GPL source release, so users must supply their own files. hel1o-wor1d/OpenRA2 links a OneDrive download of the game, which is likely unauthorized; do not use or propagate it. A GPLv3 web deployment requires publishing all engine and mod source.
C# with a YAML trait system is a very different skill stack from the JS/TS web candidates. Mixing both routes would split effort.
score_rationale:
3/10 for OpenRA/ra2; 1/10 for hel1o-wor1d/OpenRA2, a README-only fork that is behind upstream and carries a legal red flag.

**Points in favour:**
- Clean GPLv3 licensing.
- A mature, actively maintained engine with excellent multiplayer, lobby, replay, save, editor and fog infrastructure.
- Most RA2 units and superweapons already present.
- Proven HD-sprite and post-processing capability upstream (TiberianDawnHD, release-20250330).
- A GLES3 renderer that maps well onto WebGL2.

**Points against, given what this project wants (a web version first, then a faithful original experience, then 2026-level 2.5D HD):**
- It is desktop-only. A browser version means porting a whole C# engine to WASM, replacing its networking, Lua and threads, which no one has open-sourced.
- The RA2 mod lacks both campaigns, all of YR, a competent AI, FMV, garrisoning and INI compatibility.
- It is dormant, pinned to a 2023 engine without post-processing, and crashes on at least one map.
- Every advanced visual feature (water, normal-mapped lighting, particles) requires an engine fork.

**Where it is useful:**
- As a reference: its RA2 trait semantics and YAML data, the TD-HD pipeline design, and post-process pass design.
- As a desktop fallback if every web base proves unusable.

It should not be the primary base.
